hook.situation: You are viewing a studio through a real-estate office and need to ask the questions that change the real cost: deposit, monthly rent, maintenance fee, included utilities, options, and contract details.
objectives: Ask about 보증금, 월세, 관리비, and what is included.
Describe the room and layout with housing nouns and adjective modifiers.
Use 조건, 가능, 목적, and 준비 patterns for real housing decisions.
hook.whyItMatters: Housing Korean is full of words that come as a set. 원룸 without 보증금, 월세, 관리비, 포함되다, and 계약서 is not enough for the real task.

grammarNotes.title: N이/가 있어요 — what the place has
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 있어요 to list useful things in the room or building: 인터넷, 세탁기, 베란다, 엘리베이터.
grammarNotes.formation: N이/가 있어요. Use 이 after consonants and 가 after vowels.

examples.en: This studio has a balcony.
There is a refrigerator in the kitchen.
Internet is included in the maintenance fee.
There is a washing machine next to the entrance.

exceptions: For included fees, the included item is the subject: 인터넷이 포함돼 있어요, not 관리비가 인터넷을 포함해요 in beginner housing speech.

grammarNotes.title: N이/가 없어요 — missing feature or no extra fee
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 없어요 is practical in housing because missing features and missing fees both matter.
grammarNotes.formation: N이/가 없어요. Use it for absence, not refusal.

examples.en: This studio does not have a balcony.
There is no elevator.
There is no extra maintenance fee.
The contract has no internet details.

exceptions: Do not use 안 있어요 as the main learner form for absence. 없어요 is the natural negative existence word.

grammarNotes.title: A-ㄴ/은 N — describing listings
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Korean housing descriptions usually package the description before the noun: 넓은 원룸, 깨끗한 화장실.
grammarNotes.formation: Adjective stem + ㄴ/은 + noun. 하다 adjectives usually become 한: 조용한, 깨끗한.

examples.en: I am looking for a spacious studio.
It would be nice if it is a bright room.
I want a quiet neighborhood.
A clean bathroom is important.

exceptions: Do not overuse separate sentences like 원룸이 넓어요 only. 넓은 원룸 lets you describe and identify the place at once.

grammarNotes.title: A/V면 — housing conditions
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 면 is for decision points: if the fee is separate, if internet is included, if you like the room.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 면/으면 to the predicate. Use it before the decision or result.

examples.en: If the maintenance fee is separate, the rent feels expensive.
It is good if internet is included.

examples.ko: 마음에 들면 오늘 계약할 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: maeume deulmyeon oneul gyeyakal su isseoyo.
examples.en: If you like it, you can sign the contract today.
If jeonse feels burdensome, I will look at monthly-rent studios.

exceptions: 면 sets a condition. Do not use it when you simply list a fact: 보증금은 500만 원이에요, not 보증금이면 500만 원이에요.

grammarNotes.title: Vㄹ/을 수 있어요 — possibility in housing
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 수 있어요 for practical possibility: can sign, can move, can use internet, can see the room.
grammarNotes.formation: Vowel stem + ㄹ 수 있어요; consonant stem + 을 수 있어요.

examples.en: Can I sign the contract today?
I can move this week.
You can use the internet right away.
Can I see the room today?

exceptions: 수 있어요 is possibility, not desire. 보고 싶어요 means want to see; 볼 수 있어요 means can see.

grammarNotes.title: V-기 위해(서) — planned housing purpose
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 위해서 when the action has a clear purpose: finding a place, lowering rent, checking the contract.
grammarNotes.formation: Verb stem + 기 위해(서). Noun + 을/를 위해(서).

examples.en: I went to a real-estate office to find a place.

examples.ko: 월세를 줄이기 위해 작은 원룸을 보고 있어요.
examples.romanization: wolser-eul jurigi wihae jageun wollumeul bogo isseoyo.
examples.en: I am looking at a small studio to lower rent.
I brought my ID to sign the contract.
I checked the contract in order to move.

exceptions: For casual intention, -(으)려고 is often lighter. 위해서 sounds more planned or formal, which fits contracts and housing goals.

grammarNotes.title: V-아/어 두다 — prepare and leave it ready
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Housing has many before-signing tasks. 두다 says you do something now so it stays ready later.
grammarNotes.formation: Verb stem + 아/어 두다. 놓다 is similar; 두다 often feels practical and prepared.

examples.en: Check the contract in advance.
Write down the maintenance fee details.
It is good to take room photos in advance.
I set the moving date in advance.

exceptions: 아/어 두다 is intentional preparation. 아/어 있다 describes a resulting state, such as 문이 열려 있어요.

exampleSentence.en: How much is the deposit for this studio?
I went to a real-estate office to find a place.
exampleSentence.note: In daily speech, 부동산 often means the office.
Must be asked together with 월세.

exampleSentence.en: I am looking for a monthly-rent studio rather than jeonse.

exampleSentence.note: Small word that changes total cost.

exampleSentence.en: Internet is included in the maintenance fee.

exampleSentence.note: Prepared action before signing or moving.

exampleSentence.en: You can sign the contract today.
exampleSentence.note: Real-estate action after checking the listing.

exampleSentence.en: There is a refrigerator in the kitchen.
I asked the licensed agent about the maintenance fee.
exampleSentence.note: The person helping with the contract.

extendedDialogue.setting: A tenant checks rent, deposit, utilities, and contract preparation at a real-estate office.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How much is the deposit for this studio?
lines.grammarNote: 원룸 and 보증금 belong together in listing questions.

lines.speaker: 중개사
lines.en: The deposit is 5 million won and the monthly rent is 700,000 won.
lines.grammarNote: 은/는 separates the two money topics clearly.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is the maintenance fee separate? Is internet included too?
lines.grammarNote: 따로 and 포함되다 are the key fee-boundary words.

lines.speaker: 중개사
lines.en: The maintenance fee is 70,000 won, and internet is included.
lines.grammarNote: 인터넷 is the subject of 포함돼 있어요.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 이사하기 전에 계약서를 확인해 두면 되죠?
lines.romanization: isahagi jeone gyeyakseoreul hwaginhae dumyeon doejyo?
lines.en: I should check the contract before moving, right?
lines.grammarNote: 확인해 두다 means check it in advance and keep it ready.

lines.speaker: 중개사
lines.ko: 네. 마음에 들면 오늘 계약할 수 있어요.
lines.romanization: ne. maeume deulmyeon oneul gyeyakal su isseoyo.
lines.en: Yes. If you like it, you can sign the contract today.
lines.grammarNote: 면 sets the condition; ㄹ 수 있어요 gives possibility.

readingText.title: 관리비에 인터넷이 포함돼 있어요?
readingText.body: 하나는 이사하기 위해 부동산에 갔어요. 공인중개사는 넓은 원룸 하나를 보여 줬어요. 보증금은 500만 원이고 월세는 70만 원이었어요. 하나는 관리비가 따로인지, 인터넷이 관리비에 포함돼 있는지 물어봤어요. 베란다는 없었지만 부엌에 냉장고와 세탁기가 있었고 화장실도 깨끗했어요. 마음에 들면 오늘 계약할 수 있다고 해서, 하나는 계약하기 전에 계약서를 다시 확인해 두었어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Hana went to a real-estate office to move. The licensed agent showed her a spacious studio. The deposit was 5 million won and the monthly rent was 700,000 won. Hana asked whether the maintenance fee was separate and whether internet was included in the fee. There was no balcony, but there was a refrigerator and washing machine in the kitchen, and the bathroom was clean. Since she could sign the contract that day if she liked it, Hana checked the contract again before signing.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 하나가 확인한 비용 두 가지는 뭐예요?

culturalNote.title: The real cost is not only 월세
culturalNote.body: In Korean rentals, 월세 is only one part of the monthly burden. 보증금 is paid up front, 관리비 may be separate, and utilities such as internet, water, gas, or electricity may or may not be included. A good housing conversation checks all of these before 계약하다.
culturalNote.tip: Ask in this order: 보증금이 얼마예요? 월세가 얼마예요? 관리비는 따로예요? 뭐가 포함돼 있어요? 계약서 먼저 확인해도 돼요?

inlineExercises.prompt: At a real-estate office, which pair belongs together?
options: 포크 세 개 / 커피 두 잔
inlineExercises.explanation: 보증금 and 월세 are core housing price terms.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which question checks whether a fee is separate?
inlineExercises.explanation: 따로 means separately and is essential for fee questions.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence asks whether internet is included?
inlineExercises.explanation: The included item is the subject, and 관리비 takes 에.

inlineExercises.prompt: Before moving, the prepared-action sentence is:
inlineExercises.explanation: -아/어 두세요 means do it in advance and leave it prepared.
Vㄹ/을 수 있어요 expresses practical possibility.

bullets: Cost set: 보증금, 월세, 관리비, 따로, 포함되다.
Housing nouns: 원룸, 거실, 부엌, 화장실, 베란다, 현관.
Listing descriptions: 넓은 원룸, 밝은 방, 조용한 동네, 깨끗한 화장실.
Decision patterns: 마음에 들면, 계약할 수 있어요, 집을 구하기 위해, 확인해 두세요.
Contract habit: check 계약서 before 계약하다.
